title: Chopin: the melody he loved most
narrativeStyle: John's directed tour on the torus: an étude as a study of the hand, the bittersweet single voice and its falling intervals, a bridge that swells, spins and is steadied by alternating sixths, and an abridged return shown side by side

narrator.name: JohnV4
narrator.delivery: calm, grounded documentary narration, downward inflection at sentence endings

cues.text: “Never another such beautiful melody”: Chopin to his pupil Adolph Gutmann
cues.speech: Chopin told his pupil Adolph Gutmann that he had never in his life written another such beautiful melody. This is that melody: the Étude in E major, Opus 10, Number 3.

cues.text: The opening phrase: one melody on top, a quiet pulse inside the same hand
Alexej Gorlatch, at the 2009 Leeds International Piano Competition (second prize)
cues.speech: This performance is by Alexei Gorlatch, at the 2009 Leeds International Piano Competition, where he won second prize.

cues.text: An étude is a study. The right hand alone: melody in the weaker outer fingers, a soft pulse from thumb and index finger
cues.speech: An étude is a study, written to perfect one skill. Listen to the right hand alone. It plays two parts at once: the weaker outer fingers sing the melody, while the thumb and index finger keep a soft pulse beneath it.

cues.text: The line climbs, each bar reaching higher
cues.speech: Now the line climbs, each bar reaching higher. At the top, a single high voice begins to fall.

cues.text: Bar 17: G♯ falls a fifth, to C♯
cues.speech: Each phrase falls a fifth: G sharp to C sharp.
cues.annotationLabel: G♯ falls a fifth, to C♯

cues.text: Bar 18: a fourth lower, D♯ falls a fifth, to G♯
cues.speech: The next begins a fourth lower, on D sharp.

cues.text: Bar 19: a third lower, B falls a fifth, to E
cues.speech: Then a third lower, on B.

cues.text: Bar 20: a smaller third, G♯, and home to E
cues.speech: Then a smaller third, on G sharp, and home to E.

cues.text: The bridge, poco più animato: sixths in the right hand, rocking between two hand shapes
cues.speech: The bridge begins, a little more animated, and the étude's other skill appears: sixths. The right hand rocks between two shapes, typically thumb with ring finger, then index with little finger.

cues.text: The first swell: forte in A major, answered softly in A minor
cues.speech: Then two swells. The first rises forte in A major, and answers itself softly in A minor.

cues.text: The second swell: a step higher, then a chain of diminished chords and tritones
cues.speech: The second swell climbs a step higher, then darkens into a chain of diminished chords and tritones: notes from opposite sides of the circle of fifths.

cues.text: The climax: fortissimo near the top of the keyboard, then con bravura double sixths in both hands, spinning out of control
Repeating, alternating sixths steady the storm; the music settles onto the dominant
cues.speech: Out of the spin, the hands lock into repeating, alternating sixths, the same rocking the étude trains. It steadies the storm, and the music settles onto the dominant, waiting.

cues.text: Smorzando e rallentando: it steadies on the dominant, waiting to come home
A and A′ side by side: bars 6 to 13 are left out of the return
cues.speech: The melody returns, but notice what Chopin leaves out. After this first phrase he skips the detour and the repeat, and goes straight to the climb. The range was built the first time; now the release comes sooner.

cues.text: Straight to the climb
The single voice again: the same falling fifths, each phrase lower than the last
cues.speech: Its nickname is Tristesse: sadness. Listen again to the falling fifths.

cues.text: The sigh returns, over the chord path that opens Pachelbel's Canon: E, B, C♯ minor, G♯ minor, A
cues.speech: Beneath the sigh, the chords walk the path of Pachelbel's Canon: each bright major chord answered by a darker minor one. Bittersweet.

cues.text: The outro: the sigh an octave lower, darkened by a C natural borrowed from E minor, then home
cues.speech: In the outro the sigh returns an octave lower, darkened by a C natural borrowed from E minor. Twice it sighs; the third time the shadow lifts, and the melody comes home.
cues.annotationLabel: C natural, borrowed from E minor

cues.text: E major
